The details show that both output and new order inflows increased at the same solid pace as recorded in July, though the August improvement in demand was the joint-strongest since November last year.

Besides that, employment expanded for the first time in the year-to-date, supported by another month of solid and broad-based sales growth.

As for price pressures, they were once again more stable with input cost pressures nudging down a fraction and output prices increasing at the same pace as in July.

However, inflation rates remained high by historical standards and were above those seen immediately prior to the US-Iran conflict.

That continues to signal that inflation risks are still present, but at least not spiraling out of control for now.

But as the US-Iran conflict rages on for longer, the risks of higher price pressures becoming more embedded into inflation expectations is something that the ECB will have to be mindful of.

As such, the central bank will look to raise interest rates again this month in order to position themselves better for the inflation battle that is to come.

As such, headline annual inflation is seen doubling in August compared to July.

However, there was only a slight increase in core annual inflation.

And this is the more important metric, one that the SNB looks at more closely to decide on monetary policy setting.

For now, the big picture outlook remains that Switzerland is still sitting very close to the bottom of the SNB’s 0% to 2% definition of price stability.

So, they are not in a hurry to move on policy in order to address the inflation situation - unlike most major economies.

The key complication for the SNB at the moment is the franc currency itself.

As a safe-haven currency, renewed geopolitical tensions can drive further appreciation in the franc.
